newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner chief sees marked rise in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner chief sees marked rise in 1996 profit.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG chief executive Juergen Sarrazin on Monday repeated his forecast for a double-digit rise in operating profit this year at Germany's second largest commercial bank.

Referring to the bank's 44 percent surge in operating earnings in the first six months, Sarrazin said: "We should not annualise the growth rate. The third quarter was particularly not as strong as the first quarter..."

"But I can still say today that I can expect markedly increased operating profit for the whole year. I would say it is going to be two-digit growth," he added. Sarrazin was speaking in a television interview with CNBC.
The Dresdner chief had made a similar forecast at a news conference in August.

Sarrazin also said the bank had not experienced problems on the lines of the crisis at rival Deutsche Bank AG's London based funds firm MGAM, which is at the centre of a probe regarding suspected illicit trading.
"Our systems are working well and we have not had any problems in our various units," he said.
"Of course we have to admit that events like that are damaging for the whole industry," he said of the MGAM disaster.
On the bank's domestic ambitions, Sarrazin indicated that the bank might soon consider following its competitors into the direct banking arena.
"We never wanted to be pioneers in this. I wanted to wait and see what the experience of others was," he said, adding that: "We now have a more mature market."
